<div id="tm-what-box" style="border: 1px solid #a2a9b1; margin-bottom: 15px; background: #ffffff; color:#202122;">
<h2 id="tm-what-h2" style="margin: 0; padding: 8px 10px; background-color: #cef2e0; border-bottom: 1px solid #a2a9b1; font-size: 1.2em; font-weight: bold;">What this registry is</h2>
<div id="tm-what" style="padding: 10px;">
Version 2 of the Principia Machina restates the framework in '''Lean 4''', a language in which proofs are checked by machine. Lean, its build tool Lake and its mathematics library Mathlib already use many of the words version 1 used every day. In Lean the ''kernel'' is the proof checker, an ''environment'' is everything defined so far, and a ''module'' is a source file; Mathlib has ''measures'' and ''manifolds''. A version 2 text that used those words bare would mean two things at once.

This registry records how each version 1 term carries over. A row gives the version 1 term; the version 2 word that replaces it, or "unchanged"; its three-letter code, where it has one; the Lean namespace where it lives in the Lean sources; and the collision the new word avoids, or the rule that settles it. Every term of version 1's framework that has no row here is carried into version 2 unchanged.

The move is declared, term by term; it is not a search and replace. Version 1's records, digests and version numbers are not changed, and version 1's pages keep version 1's words. In version 2, '''words are the names''', in prose and in the Lean sources alike. A three-letter code is an abbreviation for tables, digest labels and page titles, and is used nowhere a word fits.
</div>
</div>

<div id="tm-codes-box" style="border: 1px solid #a2a9b1; margin-bottom: 15px; background: #ffffff; color:#202122;">
<h2 id="tm-codes-h2" style="margin: 0; padding: 8px 10px; background-color: #ffedad; border-bottom: 1px solid #a2a9b1; font-size: 1.2em; font-weight: bold;">The codes are approved</h2>
<div id="tm-codes" style="padding: 10px;">
'''The three-letter codes on this page are approved.''' The Declarer approved the code table on 15 October 2026, once and as a whole, as it had been proposed. A code added to the table later is proposed until the Declarer approves it.

The codes were drawn up under rule R8 below: any two differ in at least two letters and none is a Lean core type, and a code that is also a known acronym elsewhere is flagged in its row. A note such as "not PRS (one letter from PFS)" records a candidate code that failed the rule.
</div>
</div>

<div id="tm-table-box" style="border: 1px solid #a2a9b1; margin-bottom: 15px; background: #ffffff; color:#202122;">
<h2 id="tm-table-h2" style="margin: 0; padding: 8px 10px; background-color: #cedff2; border-bottom: 1px solid #a2a9b1; font-size: 1.2em; font-weight: bold;">The registry</h2>
<div id="tm-table" style="padding: 10px;">
One row per term, in the order of the terminology map this page is generated from. A blank cell means the map gives nothing there: the term has no code, or no Lean namespace of its own. "none" in the code column means the word deliberately has no code and is always written in full. Rules are cited by number (R1 to R9, [[#tm-rules-box|below]]); a row that avoids a Mathlib word binds only under rule R7.

<div id="tm-rules-box" style="border: 1px solid #a2a9b1; margin-bottom: 15px; background: #ffffff; color:#202122;">
<h2 id="tm-rules-h2" style="margin: 0; padding: 8px 10px; background-color: #cef2e0; border-bottom: 1px solid #a2a9b1; font-size: 1.2em; font-weight: bold;">The naming rules</h2>
<div id="tm-rules" style="padding: 10px;">
Nine rules govern every version 2 name. The registry's last column cites them by number.

# '''R1. Wire names and Lean names.''' A record field, state or code keeps its capital spelling on pages, in records and in prose (<code>UNIT</code>, <code>AT</code>, <code>MATCH</code>). In Lean the same thing is a lowerCamel word that is not a Lean keyword (<code>unit</code>, <code>atPoint</code>, <code>outcome</code>). One table maps each wire name to its Lean name; no name is escaped to get past a keyword.
# '''R2. No bare colliding word.''' A word that clashes seriously with a meaning in Lean, Lake or Mathlib is never used alone. It is written as a two-word compound, in prose and in code, and Lean's own sense is always qualified: "the Lean kernel" when Lean's proof checker is meant.
# '''R3. Every layer and zone is a namespace.''' Each layer and zone of the framework is a namespace under <code>Principia</code>, such as <code>Principia.StartingSet</code>. No single-word framework type sits at the root, and nothing shadows a Lean, Lake or Mathlib type.
# '''R4. Digest, not hash.''' Every SHA-256 value is a digest. "Hash" is left to Lean's own 64-bit <code>hash</code> and to MediaWiki's SHA-1 of a page, which version 2 text calls the page digest.
# '''R5. No type named like a Lean type.''' No framework type is named Name, Option, Unit, Level, Position, Format, Json, Declaration, Module, Environment, Kernel, Task, Job, Package, Workspace, Manifest, Target, Script, Cache, Env or Int.
# '''R6. A registry.''' This page: every version 1 term with its version 2 word, code, Lean name, collision and rule. The move is declared, term by term, not done by search and replace, and version 1's records, digests and version numbers are not changed.
# '''R7. Mathlib rows are conditional.''' A row that avoids a Mathlib word binds only if version 2 adopts Mathlib, Lean's mathematics library. Version 2 is written in core Lean for now, by the Declarer's choice; a later move to Mathlib would be a change of its own, and the rows are recorded now so that it is made with them in view.
# '''R8. Codes.''' Any two codes differ in at least two letters, so a one-letter slip cannot turn one into another. No code is a Lean core type, and none is a well-known acronym in computing, cryptography or physics; where an overlap remains, the row says so.
# '''R9. The size test.''' A name must read right for a spring on a track: nothing may sound too big for the smallest system the framework is used on.
</div>
</div>

<div id="tm-new-box" style="border: 1px solid #a2a9b1; margin-bottom: 15px; background: #ffffff; color:#202122;">
<h2 id="tm-new-h2" style="margin: 0; padding: 8px 10px; background-color: #cedff2; border-bottom: 1px solid #a2a9b1; font-size: 1.2em; font-weight: bold;">How a new term gets a row</h2>
<div id="tm-new" style="padding: 10px;">
Every term of version 1's framework that is not listed here is carried into version 2 unchanged until a row says otherwise. Nothing is renamed silently.

When the work meets a term that needs a new word, most often because Lean, Lake or Mathlib already uses it, a row is added to the terminology map with all five columns:
# the version 1 term, as version 1 wrote it;
# the version 2 word, checked against Lean, Lake and Mathlib (R2, R3, R5) and against the size test (R9);
# a code, only if the word needs one, checked under R8 against every code already in the table; a new code is proposed until the Declarer approves it;
# the Lean namespace, under <code>Principia</code> (R3);
# the collision the word avoids, or the rule applied.
This page is then generated again from the map and checked against it row by row, so the page and the map cannot differ. Like every framework page, it reaches this wiki only after the Declarer approves the change.
</div>
</div>
